name: 2026-08-11-dedup-factdrift

items.text: The team is reworking memory from flat fact-buckets into a two-tier system: a narrative base plus a relational base that records the reasons and context behind decisions, because the boss wants ChatGPT-style long-term memory.
An index layer over meeting notes is needed so search is efficient and cuts token cost, especially for long meetings and complex queries.
The user automated version tracking across web, mobile, MCP, and backend so each service increments its own version.
The 50MB upload limit was a Supabase free-tier cap; it was fixed by upgrading to Supabase Pro, and the cap is now 200MB.
Recording is capped at 2 hours and the audio bitrate was raised to 64kbps (it had been lowered earlier to fit a 50MB/2-hour budget, no longer a hard constraint after the Supabase Pro upgrade).
Speaker diarization should move from pure voice-pattern matching to context-based identification using accumulated per-person memory, with an alpha/beta targeted for next Wednesday.
The user-profile ontology (built by Jin) should auto-update as memory accumulates so a person's role and relationships get clearer over time, instead of being redefined per meeting.
Meeting memory belongs to the user (not the note) and accumulates chronologically per user, so it builds into a per-person knowledge base.
The app package is being renamed from com.example.* to com.tecace.* to enable Azure MS Authentication; the source rename is waiting on the Korea developer.
The MCP server had a critical fail-open auth hole and a transcript-flag bug; both were fixed and verified in prod.
iOS release goes through TGX's account; each build lasts about a week and currently needs a manual rebuild and reinstall.
The admin/monitoring dashboard is a separate Vercel site; the user's account lacks permission and it sits on someone's personal account, needing an org transfer.
